content: The inch of mercury (inHg or Hg) is a non-SI unit used to measure pressure. It remains widely utilized in the United States for reporting barometric pressure in weather forecasts and aviation, although it is considered somewhat outdated in other parts of the world. This unit is defined as the pressure exerted by a column of mercury that is one inch in height at a temperature of 32°F (0°C) under standard gravitational acceleration. In aviation, altimeter readings derived from this unit are referred to as flight levels. Additionally, piston-engine aircraft equipped with constant-speed propellers use inches of mercury to measure manifold pressure, which serves as an indicator of the engine's power output.
